Command: Do All to the Glory of God
Summary: Paul's glory command: whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
Commandment: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.
Application: Set at the end of the idol-food discussion, this lifts the whole question beyond permission: the test of any act, even eating and drinking, is whether God is glorified by it.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to make God's glory the final test of ordinary acts, not only of religious ones.
Function: Even eating and drinking are tested by God's glory. An apostolic command, not a Mosaic one — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal, on the TRADITIONAL reading, was to make God's glory the final test of ordinary acts, not only of religious ones. The evil it addressed was permission-seeking that stops at what is allowed and never asks what glorifies God. It restrained that evil by the test itself: whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
